thread.title: General Electric Is Now Smaller Than Each of the FANG Stocks by Market Value

author: thestreet.com
title: General Electric Is Now Smaller Than Each of the FANG Stocks by Market Value
text:
How the mighty have fallen.
General Electric Co. ( GE ) , once the most valuable company in the U.S., is now smaller than all of the FANG firms by market value.
FANG, an acronym coined by TheStreet's founder and Action Alerts Plus portfolio manager Jim Cramer, refers to tech darlings Facebook Inc. ( FB ) , Amazon.com Inc. ( AMZN ) , Netflix Inc. ( NFLX ) and Alphabet Inc. ( GOOGL ) .
GE ceded its spot as the most valuable company in the world in 2005, when Exxon Mobil Corp. ( XOM ) took the lead. But before then, General Electric had led the pack by market cap for at least six of the previous nine years. After Exxon overtook GE by market cap, though, GE still remained in the top three for the next five years.
Now, General Electric doesn't break the top 10 by a long shot. Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) is the most valuable company in the world with a market cap most recently of $853.44 billion.
General Electric's market cap was $112.45 billion on Monday, March 26. Facebook had a market value at that time of $441.59 billion. Amazon's was $735.06 billion, Alphabet's was $714.13 billion and Netflix, the smallest in the group, had a market share of $133.04 billion. Netflix now boasts a value 18% larger than General Electric's.
In the last 12 months, shares of General Electric have spiraled downward , shedding about 56% of their value. In just the five trading days last week, GE stock fell 8.7%. On Friday, GE stock met new 52-week lows, bottoming out at $13.02 a share.
